title: Ngalakh, Thiakry Couscous with Neuteri Sauce (peko-peko)
author: peko-peko.fr (no author signed)
desc: 100 g of thiakry couscous softened with boiling water, mixed with butter, salt and raisins, then folded into a chilled sauce of 70 g baobab powder, 100 g peanut paste, sugar, vanilla and nutmeg whisked into 500 ml of water.
longDesc: Published on peko-peko.fr on 30 June 2020 as ‘Recette de ngalakh’, dessert sénégalais au baobab et beurre de cacahuète. Total time printed 30 minutes; 4 to 6 servings. THE COUSCOUS: 100 g of thiakry (medium-grain millet couscous, or standard couscous), 5 g of butter or oil, a pinch of salt and 15 g of raisins. The page tells you to cook the thiakry as the packet says or, failing that, in a microwave in 1- to 2-minute intervals with boiling water, stirring and adding water as needed; add the butter, salt and raisins while it is still hot; cool completely. THE SAUCE (neuteri): 70 g of baobab powder (or 100 g of whole baobab fruit), 100 g of peanut paste, 50 g sugar or to taste, half a teaspoon of vanilla extract or a sachet of vanilla sugar, an optional teaspoon of Nutella, one eighth of a teaspoon of nutmeg and 500 ml of water. If you use whole grains or a powder full of lumps, boil the baobab in the 500 ml of water and simmer 10 minutes, then strain through a fine sieve; the step is skipped with a ready-to-dilute powder. Mix the peanut paste, sugar, Nutella, vanilla and nutmeg, whisk in the baobab juice little by little, and chill until well cold. Mix couscous into the sauce at serving time.
ingredients: 100 g thiakry (medium millet couscous, from an African grocer) or standard couscous, large grain if possible
70 g baobab powder, or 100 g baobab fruit in grains
100 g peanut paste, smooth peanut butter or peanut puree
1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract, or 1 sachet vanilla sugar
steps: If you are using whole baobab grains, or a powder still full of lumps, boil the baobab in the 500 ml of water and simmer 10 minutes, stirring, then strain through a fine sieve. With a ready-to-dilute powder, skip this step.
Mix the peanut paste, sugar, Nutella (if using), vanilla and nutmeg. Whisk in the baobab juice little by little. Refrigerate until well chilled.
Rehydrate the raisins in a small bowl of boiling water (no time is printed).

Cook the thiakry as the packet says or, failing that, in the microwave in 1- to 2-minute intervals with boiling water, stirring and adding water as needed. The page’s boiling-water step is read two ways (see the notes): about 130 g of boiling water on the 100 g of thiakry, covered and rested 15 minutes, in one reading; no quantity or rest in the other.
Add the butter, salt and the drained raisins while the couscous is still hot. Cool completely.
At serving time, mix the couscous into the chilled sauce.
chefTips: Printed cues (single reading): the couscous should be « bien tendre » and « s’écraser facilement entre les doigts »; the baobab pieces should « se désagréger ».
The author distinguishes pâte d’arachide, the African peanut puree (often salted and emulsified), from peanut butter.
Keep couscous and sauce separate in the refrigerator and reheat the couscous briefly before mixing with the chilled sauce.
commonMistakes: Mixing couscous and sauce long before serving.
Treating the 130 g / 15-minute reading as settled: the second reading of the page omits both.
storage: Couscous and sauce are kept separately in the refrigerator; no time is printed.
reheating: Reheat the couscous briefly before mixing with the chilled sauce.
healthBenefits: Baobab adds vitamin C; peanut paste adds protein.
culturalNote: The page ties ngalakh to Easter: the Christian minority prepares large quantities on Good Friday for neighbours and guests, including Muslims, making it a symbol of interfaith fraternity; in 2020 the health crisis disrupted this sharing. Baobab fruit is ‘pain de singe’ or ‘bouye’ in Senegal.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Recette de ngalakh’, ‘Dessert sénégalais au baobab et beurre de cacahuète’. NO AUTHOR SIGNED — comments are signed ‘PekoPeko’ (the site name); flagged. Date: 30/06/2020. Yield ‘4 à 6 personnes’ (5 used). Total time printed 30 minutes. TWO-PASS on the ingredient list.

DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN PASSES, reported and not resolved: pass 1 gave the couscous step as ‘verser environ 130 g d’eau bouillante sur les 100 g de thiakry, couvrir et laisser reposer 15 minutes’; pass 2 omitted both the 130 g and the 15-minute rest. The ingredient quantities agreed across passes.

Cues (pass 1 only, SINGLE-PASS): « bien tendre », « s’écraser facilement entre les doigts », « se désagréger ». Times: baobab simmer 10 minutes; microwave in 1- to 2-minute intervals; raisin rehydration has NO printed time; chill ‘bien fraîche’ with no printed time. The prep/rest/cook split above is a scheduling split of the printed 30-minute total plus an assumed chill; it is not source data.
No fermentation or soaking step beyond the raisins.
